item.text: {"search_note":"I found strong 2024 evidence on AI and cyber, but no reliable 2024 evidence on biological-risk governance from Kishida’s public record. I also did not find evidence that he was unusually transparent about all dual-use decisions; the transparency signal is strongest in the AI code-of-conduct / reporting-style governance, not in the security side. Best reading: yes on precaution and institutionalization in AI/cyber; mixed because those same domains were also used to justify hard-security buildup.","evidence":[{"title":"Speech by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio at the Generative AI Side Event","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"May 2, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202405/02ai.html","summary":"Kishida said generative AI has serious downsides such as disinformation, called for international governance for “safe, secure, and trustworthy AI,” and said Japan would support technical measures like content-origin verification. This is direct precaution-and-transparency evidence.","question_ids":["1B.9","1B.4","1B.8"]},{"title":"Prime Minister Kishida’s Participation in the AI Seoul Summit Leaders’ Session (Video Message) (Summary)","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"May 21, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/diplomatic/202405/21aisummit.html","summary":"Kishida said international governance was urgently needed to mitigate AI risks and reiterated that the Hiroshima AI Process produced guiding principles and a code of conduct, with a Friends Group to advance implementation. That is strong evidence of precaution plus multilateral transparency.","question_ids":["1B.9","1B.4","1B.7"]},{"title":"Speech by Prime Minister Kishida at the “Future of Asia” Forum","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"May 23, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202405/23speech.html","summary":"Kishida said Japan would strengthen the foundations of digital technology, including cybersecurity, and cited the Hiroshima AI Process Friends Group as a 49-country framework. He framed the work as expert-led and institution-building, which supports precaution, though the policy itself is security-hardening.","question_ids":["1B.9","1B.7","1B.8"]},{"title":"Policy Speech by Prime Minister Kishida to the 213th Session of the Diet","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"January 30, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html","summary":"Kishida said Japan would enhance security clearances and cyber security and accelerate a bill to build the domestic legal structure. That is evidence of formalized safeguards and legal preparation for cyber risk management.","question_ids":["1B.9","1B.7"]},{"title":"Policy Speech by Prime Minister Kishida to the 213th Session of the Diet","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"January 30, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html","summary":"In the same speech, Kishida described Japan’s security environment as severe and committed to strengthening defense capabilities and counterstrike capability. This shows robust strategic coordination, but it is also a sign that dual-use capabilities were being integrated into alliance competition and security alignment.","question_ids":["1B.9","1B.4","1B.8"]}]}
